# Results — Study 698 (ABCD-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**the AB=CD harmonic predicts the reversal at point D**: three confirmed swing pivots
A, B, C where the retracement leg BC pulls back **61.8%** of the impulse leg AB, project
a fourth point **D = C + AB** ("AB=CD", the extension leg equals the impulse leg), and
expect price to *reverse* the moment it touches D. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ,
AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to sibling
[77-golden-mean](../../77-golden-mean/), for apples-to-apples comparison.*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 3%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Fibonacci arm | BC retraces AB by **0.618 ± 0.10**; projects **D = C + ext × AB** with **ext = 1.0 ± 0.15** ("AB=CD") |
| Placebo arm | identical pivots, but each candidate's retrace/extension *targets* are drawn uniformly at random (retrace ∈ [0.25, 0.90], ext ∈ [0.5, 2.0]), kept clear of the Fibonacci band under test — "any equal-legged reversal projection", seeded deterministically per candidate |
| D-touch scan | forward window of **40 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range brackets D (or closes within 0.75% of it) |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — a standard technical-signal convention, identical in both arms, documented once) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0 (events can cluster in time); Welch *t* for the Fibonacci-vs-placebo arm comparison; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named —
not a membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Fibonacci ABCD vs the placebo, pooled across the basket

Pooled confirmed pivots: **4,200** → Fibonacci ABCD candidates: **528** (touched: 349) →
placebo candidates: **523** (touched: 252).

| horizon | arm | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* | Fib − Plac Welch *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | Fibonacci | 349 | 50.1% | −6.89 | −0.35 | −0.24 |
| 1-day  | Placebo   | 252 | 52.0% | +0.06 | +0.00 | |
| **5-day (headline)** | **Fibonacci** | **349** | **45.3%** | **−45.29** | **−1.18** | **−1.49** |
| 5-day  | Placebo   | 252 | 54.8% | +41.54 | +1.06 | |
| 10-day | Fibonacci | 349 | 41.8% | −79.18 | −1.49 | −1.68 |
| 10-day | Placebo   | 252 | 54.0% | +63.94 | +0.95 | |

Hit rate (5-day): Fibonacci **45.3%** (Wilson 95% [40.1%, 50.5%]) vs placebo **54.8%**
(Wilson [48.6%, 60.8%]).

- **Neither arm clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, in either direction.** The Fibonacci
  arm's point estimate is *negative* at every horizon — fading at a completed AB=CD
  costs money on average, not earns it — but it is not statistically distinguishable
  from zero (|*t*| ≤ 1.49).
- **The placebo arm is not "the bounce" either** — its mean is positive but equally
  uncertified (*t* ≤ 1.06). Neither arm shows the mean-reversion structure a believer
  would predict.
- **The Fibonacci arm does not beat the placebo at any horizon** (Welch *t* between
  −0.24 and −1.68) — if anything the reverse: at the headline 5-day horizon Fibonacci
  underperforms the random-ratio control by **86.8 bps/event**. There is no Fibonacci
  specificity: whatever a random equal-legged reversal projection captures, the
  0.618/1.0 harmonic pair does not capture *more* of it.

## Per-instrument (5-day, gross)

| Ticker | Fib *n* | Fib mean (bps) | Fib *t* | Plac *n* | Plac mean (bps) | Plac *t* | Fib beats Plac? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| SPY  | 36 | −73.25  | −1.09 | 16 | +96.22  | +1.21 | no |
| QQQ  | 39 | +61.53  | +1.11 | 29 | +10.47  | +0.14 | **yes** |
| AAPL | 71 | −53.57  | −0.88 | 44 | +81.95  | +1.14 | no |
| MSFT | 47 | +2.80   | +0.06 | 40 | +152.56 | +1.70 | no |
| TSLA | 59 | **−283.57** | **−2.12** | 61 | −21.68  | −0.21 | no |
| NVDA | 97 | +49.83  | +0.64 | 62 | +3.84   | +0.05 | **yes** |

Fibonacci beats the placebo on only **2 of 6** tickers (QQQ, NVDA). The single
individually significant result on the whole board is **TSLA's fade at *t* = −2.12** —
and it is significant in the *wrong* direction: fading a completed AB=CD on TSLA lost
money reliably, the opposite of the claim.

## The fade-at-D timer, net of costs (5-day hold)

| round-trip cost | Fibonacci net mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −45.29 | −1.18 |
| 5.0 bps  | −55.29 | −1.45 |
| 10.0 bps | −65.29 | −1.71 |

Costs only push an already-negative point estimate further negative (the Fib-vs-Plac
Welch *t* is unchanged at −1.49 by a shared cost, since costs subtract identically from
both arms). There is no cost level at which the fade turns attractive — it starts
negative and gets worse.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA),
pooled across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample
size); no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~285/seed | — | mean **−0.37** (sd 0.90), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.08` (seed 698) | 357 | +133.81 | **+9.35** |

The detector fires at the nominal ~5% false-positive rate on the null and lights up
sharply on a planted mean-reversion tendency — the pipeline can find a real AB=CD
reversal effect when one is actually there. *(A faithful-engine / power check only;
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Fibonacci ABCD arm's 5-day fade-at-D return is **−45.29
  bps/event, HAC *t* = −1.18** — negative, and nowhere near the *t* ≥ 2 bar at any
  horizon (1/5/10-day: −0.35 / −1.18 / −1.49). The one individually significant number
  on the whole board (TSLA, *t* = −2.12) points *against* the claim, not for it.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The fade loses money before costs and loses more after
  them (−45.29 → −65.29 bps/event as one-way cost rises 0 → 10 bps). There is no
  regime in this sweep where the trade is attractive.
- **"Beats a random equal-legged reversal projection?" — BUSTED.** The Fibonacci arm
  underperforms the seeded placebo at every horizon tested (Welch *t* from −0.24 to
  −1.68) and beats it on only 2 of 6 tickers. The 0.618 retracement / AB=CD extension
  pair carries no detectable specificity over an arbitrary equal-legged projection —
  consistent with sibling [77-golden-mean](../../77-golden-mean/)'s finding that
  Fibonacci ratios add nothing over placebo levels on the same six tapes.
